evidence.reference_title: Clinical features and patient management of Lujo hemorrhagic fever.
evidence.snippet: Illness typically began with the abrupt onset of fever, malaise, headache, and myalgias followed successively by sore throat, chest pain, gastrointestinal symptoms, rash, minor hemorrhage, subconjunctival injection, and neck and facial swelling over the first week of illness.

nodes.description: LUJV glycoprotein uses neuropilin-2 as a surface entry factor and the tetraspanin CD63 to stimulate pH-activated membrane fusion; human CD63 large extracellular-loop residues around phenylalanine 143 help explain why human cells are more permissive than rodent cell lines.

evidence.reference_title: NRP2 and CD63 Are Host Factors for Lujo Virus Cell Entry.
evidence.snippet: A genome-wide haploid genetic screen identified the transmembrane protein neuropilin 2 (NRP2) and tetraspanin CD63 as factors for LUJV GP-mediated infection.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular Mechanisms Underlying the Cellular Entry and Host Range Restriction of Lujo Virus.
evidence.snippet: By site-directed mutagenesis, we further determined that a phenylalanine at position 143 in human CD63 was the key residue for efficient membrane fusion and VSVΔG*-LUJV/GP infection.

nodes.description: LUJV production depends on Z-protein late domains for efficient particle release and on site 1 protease cleavage of the glycoprotein precursor at RKLM to mature the viral entry complex.

evidence.reference_title: Analysis of Assembly and Budding of Lujo Virus.
evidence.snippet: The L domains in Z are required for efficient virus-like particle release, but Tsg101, ALIX/AIP1, and Vps4A/B are unnecessary for budding.

evidence.reference_title: Analysis of Assembly and Budding of Lujo Virus.
evidence.snippet: LUJV GPC is cleaved by site 1 protease (S1P) at the RKLM motif, and treatment with the S1P inhibitor PF-429242 reduced LUJV production.
